Solutions are included to make the resource useful for independent study. They are **selected worked solutions**, not a complete instructor marking scheme. In particular, numerical answers that depend on the installed `refugees` package version should be calculated in R; avoid copying a number from an older edition without checking the data. Click a panel to open it.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Chapter 1: installing versus loading"}
`install.packages("dplyr")` downloads and installs the package into the R library on your computer. You typically do that once per R installation, and again when updating. `library(dplyr)` makes the package available in the current R session. You usually run `library()` whenever you start a fresh analysis.

A project containing a script helps make your analysis reproducible because other users can run a saved sequence of commands rather than guessing what you typed at the Console.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Chapter 2: vectors, missing values and means"}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
recognitions <- c(8, 11, 3, 15, 9)
sum(recognitions)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 46
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
min(recognitions)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 3
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
max(recognitions)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 15
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
median(recognitions)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 9
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
recognitions[3] <- NA
mean(recognitions)                 # NA
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] NA
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
mean(recognitions, na.rm = TRUE)  # Uses four observed entries
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 10.75
```


:::
:::


`NA` represents a missing value, not zero. Removing missing values changes the set of observations contributing to the result. If the missing value was systematically related to outcomes, simply omitting it could distort your conclusion.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Chapter 3: what is a unit of observation?"}

- `coo_name` is the country of **origin**; `coa_name` is the country of **asylum/destination**.
- `asylum_seekers` in `population` is an end-of-year **stock** and is not the number of applications filed during that year.
- The raw `population` data have origin–destination–year records, so a destination total generally requires aggregation over origins.
- `dec_rejected` records rejected decisions; `dec_other` records other/complementary protection in the decisions table.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(refugees)
library(dplyr)

refugees::population |>
  filter(year == 2022, coa_iso == "ESP") |>
  select(year, coo_name, coa_name, refugees) |>
  head(5)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 5 × 4
   year coo_name    coa_name refugees
  <dbl> <chr>       <chr>       <dbl>
1  2022 Afghanistan Spain        2740
2  2022 Albania     Spain          19
3  2022 Algeria     Spain         180
4  2022 Angola      Spain         114
5  2022 Egypt       Spain         115
```


:::
:::

:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Chapter 4: aggregate by origin instead of destination"}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
origin_2022 <- refugees::population |>
  filter(year == 2022, !is.na(coo_iso)) |>
  group_by(coo_iso, coo_name) |>
  summarise(refugee_stock = sum(refugees, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(refugee_stock))
head(origin_2022)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 6 × 3
  coo_iso coo_name               refugee_stock
  <chr>   <chr>                          <dbl>
1 SYR     Syrian Arab Rep.             6559736
2 UKR     Ukraine                      5684177
3 AFG     Afghanistan                  5661717
4 SSD     South Sudan                  2295082
5 MMR     Myanmar                      1251618
6 COD     Dem. Rep. of the Congo        932680
```


:::
:::


We sum across **destinations** so that each row represents the refugee stock reported for one origin across recorded destinations. This is not equivalent to the number displaced **within** that origin country, and missing coverage may matter.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Chapter 5: summary statistics and the selected ten-origin sample"}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(readr)
origins <- read_csv("data/unhcr_origin_top10_2022.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

x <- origins$refugees_plus_oip / 1e6
c(mean = mean(x), median = median(x), sd = sd(x),
  min = min(x), max = max(x))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
    mean   median       sd      min      max 
3.020519 1.773350 2.481545 0.748344 6.559736 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
origins |> filter(refugees_plus_oip > mean(refugees_plus_oip))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 4 × 2
  origin                             refugees_plus_oip
  <chr>                                          <dbl>
1 Syrian Arab Rep.                             6559736
2 Ukraine                                      5684177
3 Afghanistan                                  5661717
4 Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of)           5447849
```


:::
:::


Interpret this as a description of the **selected ten** origin countries, not the average over all origins. If a few observations are especially large, mean and median can differ.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Chapter 6: make a top-ten destination plot"}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(ggplot2)
hosts <- refugees::population |>
  filter(year == 2022, !is.na(coa_iso)) |>
  group_by(coa_iso, coa_name) |>
  summarise(refugee_stock = sum(refugees, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

top10 <- hosts |> slice_max(order_by = refugee_stock, n = 10)

ggplot(top10, aes(x = refugee_stock / 1e6,
                  y = reorder(coa_name, refugee_stock))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2475a6") +
  labs(x = "Reported refugee stock (millions)", y = NULL,
       title = "Ten largest destination totals in the included 2022 data",
       caption = "Source: refugees::population; check destination reporting categories") +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](solutions_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=768}
:::
:::


Changing color or theme does not change the data. Changing the measure, denominator, filtering rules, or axis may change the substantive message.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Chapter 7: an absolute change is not an arrival"}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
series <- refugees::population |>
  filter(year %in% c(2015, 2022), coa_iso %in% c("DEU", "ESP", "FRA")) |>
  group_by(coa_iso, coa_name, year) |>
  summarise(stock = sum(refugees, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

series |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = stock,
                     names_prefix = "stock_") |>
  mutate(absolute_change = stock_2022 - stock_2015,
         pct_change = if_else(stock_2015 > 0,
                              100 * (stock_2022 / stock_2015 - 1), NA_real_))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 3 × 6
  coa_iso coa_name stock_2015 stock_2022 absolute_change pct_change
  <chr>   <chr>         <dbl>      <dbl>           <dbl>      <dbl>
1 DEU     Germany      316098    2075445         1759347       557.
2 ESP     Spain          6447     314490          308043      4778.
3 FRA     France       273117     612934          339817       124.
```


:::
:::


These values describe **differences between reported end-of-year stocks**, not the count of people who arrived during the intervening period.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Chapter 8: compute the toy protection rates"}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(readr)
toy <- read_csv("data/toy_asylum_decisions.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

toy |>
  mutate(
    substantive = recognized + other_protection + rejected,
    refugee_recognition = 100 * recognized / substantive,
    total_protection = 100 * (recognized + other_protection) / substantive,
    incorrect_including_closed = 100 * (recognized + other_protection) /
      (substantive + closed)
  ) |>
  select(country, refugee_recognition, total_protection,
         incorrect_including_closed)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 5 × 4
  country refugee_recognition total_protection incorrect_including_closed
  <chr>                 <dbl>            <dbl>                      <dbl>
1 Albia                    45               60                       54.5
2 Borelia                  12               20                       17.4
3 Castria                  70               80                       76.2
4 Demeria                  30               50                       38.5
5 Estovia                  25               50                       25  
```


:::
:::


For fictional **Albia**, the recognition rate is 45%, the total protection rate is 60%, and the rate wrongly including closed in the denominator is 60/110 ≈ 54.5%. In comparative administrative data, you must define the substantive outcomes and decision level consistently.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Chapter 9: unmatched join observations"}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
stock <- refugees::population |>
  filter(year == 2022, !is.na(coa_iso)) |>
  group_by(coa_iso) |>
  summarise(stock = sum(refugees, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

apps <- refugees::asylum_applications |>
  filter(year == 2022, !is.na(coa_iso)) |>
  group_by(coa_iso) |>
  summarise(applications = sum(applied, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

joined <- left_join(stock, apps, by = "coa_iso")
sum(is.na(joined$applications))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 34
```


:::
:::


Unmatched observations are not necessarily countries with **zero** claims. Our simplified application aggregation is only for teaching joins—it is not harmonized across cases/persons or procedure types.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Chapter 10: read a regression coefficient"}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
practice <- data.frame(
  staff = c(5, 8, 10, 12, 15),
  processing_months = c(13, 12, 9, 10, 7)
)
coef(lm(processing_months ~ staff, data = practice))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
(Intercept)       staff 
 16.0620690  -0.5862069 
```


:::
:::


The slope gives a fitted **difference in months of processing time for a one-person difference in staffing**. It is not automatically the effect of *adding* a staff member: case composition and other institutional differences could be confounders.
:::

## A final note on solutions

The most important part of an answer is often its **interpretation**, not the number printed by R. For substantive research, report the target population, time period, category, procedural scope, data source, unit, exclusions and denominator.
